title: Introduce Theme Mechanism
description:
Introduce a theme mechanism. The default theme is the semio theme. In os and playgrounds add a theme tab to settings side panel where premade themes can be selected, and customized. Add save and load mechanism. All tokens are editable in tree etc.

Approach (see full plan in ticket folder / conversation): rename the existing light/dark palette dimension from "theme" to "appearance" (freeing "theme" for this new concept); build a UiTheme model covering colors, spacing, fontStacks, canvasFonts, strokes, radii, opacities, metrics, and appearances (light/dark palette groups); extend runtime merge bridges beyond colors to all tokens; add a Theme settings tab (select premades semio+mono, edit every token in a tree, save/load custom themes via localStorage + .theme.json export/import) in the shared os-shell settings panel (covers os and playgrounds/studio since they share the same shell).
summary:
Fixed: "the theme reset button doesn't reset the theme." Not a logic bug in the reset mechanism itself — I verified the draft-discard mechanism worked correctly in multiple scenarios (editing a premade, editing a saved custom theme, both before and after a page reload). The actual issue was a semantics/UX mismatch: "Reset" only discarded unsaved draft edits and was disabled whenever there was nothing to discard (`disabled={!host.themeDirty}`). If a user selected a non-default theme (e.g. a saved custom theme or a premade) without editing any tokens, the button was correctly disabled — so clicking it did nothing, which reads exactly like "the button doesn't work." Confirmed this was the actual scenario via the user's own description: theme selected, no edits made, clicked Reset, nothing happened.

Changed Reset to also revert the theme *selection* back to semio, not just discard a draft: `resetTheme` now calls `setUiThemeIdState("semio")` alongside clearing the draft, and the button's disabled condition is now `!host.themeDirty && host.themeId === "semio"` (enabled whenever there are unsaved edits OR the selection isn't already semio). Saved custom themes are untouched — only the active selection and any in-progress draft are reset.

Verified live on a fresh, self-started dev server: selected a saved custom theme ("My Test", grayscale) with no pending edits, clicked Reset, confirmed the whole UI chrome flipped back to semio's pink immediately, the theme picker showed "semio", and --color-primary / data-ui-theme / the persisted localStorage id all correctly reflect the switch. Framework-renderer-react test suite still 71/71 passing.
